text:
maria-support: Hey team, BurstLabs is hitting 500s on /v1/generate on their Dedicated cluster intermittently. They reported a correlated GPU OOM on node gpu-prod-07 around 2026-03-01T14:02Z. Customer sent these request IDs: req_20260301_az01_11a2, req_20260301_az01_11a3, req_20260301_az01_11b0. Can we get repro logs and a debug bundle?

raj-sre: Thanks — can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces (if they have it) and any pod/node names? Also we need: kubectl logs for the serving pod, dmesg/Xid if present, and nvidia-smi output around the crash.

maria-support: They gave a curl that consistently fails (~30% of requests). Here it is (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"redwood-4x-ded","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}' \\
```

Pods involved: serving-burstlabs-7f8c9 (namespace burstlabs-prod). Node: gpu-prod-07. I pulled partial logs and saw this at the end of the pod log: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating KV cache" and a proxied 500 to the API. Attaching short snippet: 

```
2026-03-01T14:01:59Z serving: step=decode tokens=512 time_ms=236
2026-03-01T14:02:03Z error: CUDA out of memory while allocating 5242880 bytes
2026-03-01T14:02:03Z proxy: returning 500 to client, request=req_20260301_az01_11a2
```

raj-sre: Ok good. Can you run these on the node (or ask infra) and attach outputs: 1) sudo dmesg | tail -n 40 2) nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-sample.csv --duration=5 3) kubectl -n burstlabs-prod logs serving-burstlabs-7f8c9 --previous --container=runtime > /tmp/serving-prev.log. Also include `kubectl describe pod` output.

maria-support: Running the collection commands now. I also created a quick repro bundle with our helper: 

```bash
redwood collect-debug --cluster dedicated-eu1 \\  --namespace burstlabs-prod \\  --pod serving-burstlabs-7f8c9 \\  --request-ids req_20260301_az01_11a2,req_20260301_az01_11a3,req_20260301_az01_11b0 \\  --include-node-logs gpu-prod-07
```

bundle-bot: I created debug bundle bundle-20260301-4573 (s3://redwood-debug/dedicated-eu1/bundle-20260301-4573.tar.gz). It contains: pod logs, kubelet logs, dmesg, nvidia-smi snapshot, and profiler traces.

oliver-eng: Thanks. Once we have the bundle I'll run a quick kernel/Xid scan and DCGM time series check. Please also grab prometheus query for gpu_memory_used_bytes for node=gpu-prod-07 between 2026-03-01T13:50Z and 2026-03-01T14:10Z and upload the CSV. If DCGM shows memory spike concurrent with the requests that's a smoking gun.

maria-support: Uploaded prom csv to the bundle path and added the following line to the ticket: "prom_query: gpu_memory_used_bytes{node=\"gpu-prod-07\"} 2026-03-01T13:50Z..2026-03-01T14:10Z -> stored in s3 path above". Also attached kubectl describe output and the short dmesg excerpt: 

```
[  121.345678] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: Unable to schedule due to OOM
[  121.345690] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU exception on chid 0x2c, reason 0x8c
```

raj-sre: Great, assigning to eng-runtime for root cause and follow-up. @oliver-eng can you triage memory accounting/quantization fallback? I'll draft a customer reply: ask them to temporarily lower max_tokens to 512 and enable KV cache truncation to avoid the OOM until we roll a fix. :eyes: :thumbsup:

oliver-eng: Will do. First pass: check whether model variant got promoted to full fp16 and whether batching policy was too aggressive for this tenant. If needed we can add a per-tenant batch cap. I'll post findings back here after analyzing the bundle. :shipit:

maria-support: Customer updated that reducing max_tokens to 512 dropped error rate to ~2%. Keeping them informed. Bundle ID and S3 link are in the ticket. Closing loop here once eng-runtime confirms root cause. Thanks everyone!
